records.independentSolutionText: (a) P(A)=0.1+p=0.3, so p=0.2. (b) The four disjoint regions total 1: 0.1+0.2+q+0.4=1, hence q=0.3. (c) A′∪B excludes only the A-only region, whose probability is 0.1. Therefore P(A′∪B)=1−0.1=0.9.

records.accessibleText: [Maximum mark: 25] This question asks you to explore curves in the complex plane defined by r = a + b sin θ, where a and b are real constants. A complex number z can be represented by a point in the complex plane whose position is determined by the modulus, r, and the argument, θ, of z. The set of points which satisfy a given relationship between r and θ form a curve in the complex plane. Consider a family of curves defined by r = a + b sin θ, where a and b are real constants. First consider the case where a = 4 and b = 0 so that r = 4. The curve defined by r = 4 is the set of points in the complex plane which represent complex numbers with a modulus of 4. (a) Suppose that z is a complex number such that r = 4. Find all possible values of z such that (i) z is purely real; [1] (ii) z is purely imaginary; [1] (iii) the argument of z is π/4. [1] (b) Sketch the curve defined by r = 4 on an Argand diagram, showing clearly the values of the intercepts with the real and imaginary axes. [2] Now consider the case where a = 0 and b = 4 so that r = 4 sin θ, where 0 ≤ θ ≤ π. (c) Suppose that z is a complex number such that r = 4 sin θ, where 0 ≤ θ ≤ π. (i) Write down the greatest possible value of r. [1] (ii) For this value of r, find z. [2] (d) Use the identities x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ to show that the points on the curve defined by r = 4 sin θ lie on the curve x² + (y − 2)² = 4, where x = Re(z) and y = Im(z). [4] The question continues on the following page. (e) Consider the curve x² + (y − 2)² = 4. (i) Find an expression for dy/dx in terms of x and y. [3] (ii) Hence or otherwise, find the values of x for which the gradient of the curve is undefined. [2] (f) The curve defined by r = 4 sin θ, where 0 ≤ θ ≤ π, is a circle. Sketch this curve on an Argand diagram, showing clearly the values of any intercepts with the real and imaginary axes. [1] Finally, consider the case where a = 4 and b = 4. The curve defined by r = 4 + 4 sin θ, where 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π, is shown on the following Argand diagram. The curve has a horizontal tangent at point A, point B and point C. The real parts of the numbers represented by A, B and C are negative, positive and zero, respectively. Diagram description: an Argand diagram with horizontal Re axis and vertical Im axis; the limacon r = 4 + 4 sin θ is drawn, passing through the origin, with a large upper loop reaching Im = 8 and extending from Re = −4 to Re = 4, and a small lower loop reaching approximately Im = −2; point A is on the lower loop at negative real part, point B is on the lower loop at positive real part, and point C is on the positive imaginary axis at Im = 8. (g) Use the identities x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ to show that the gradient of the curve at the point (r cos θ, r sin θ) is given by dy/dx = cos θ(1 + 2 sin θ)/(1 − sin θ − 2 sin² θ). [5] (h) Hence, find the value of θ which corresponds to the point A. [2]
records.independentSolutionText:
(a) (i) For r = 4, a purely real z has argument 0 or π, so z = 4e⁰ = 4 or z = 4eⁱπ = −4. Thus z = ±4.
(ii) A purely imaginary point on |z| = 4 has argument π/2 or 3π/2, so z = 4i or z = −4i. Thus z = ±4i.
(iii) If arg(z) = π/4, then z = 4(cos(π/4) + i sin(π/4)) = 4(√2/2 + i√2/2) = 2√2 + 2√2i.
(b) The locus r = 4 is the circle |z| = 4, centred at the origin with radius 4. Its intercepts are (4, 0), (−4, 0), (0, 4) and (0, −4); sketch this circle on an Argand diagram.
(c) (i) For r = 4 sin θ and 0 ≤ θ ≤ π, the greatest possible value of sin θ is 1, attained at θ = π/2. Hence r_max = 4.
(ii) At θ = π/2, z = r(cos θ + i sin θ) = 4(0 + i) = 4i.
(d) With x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ, r = 4 sin θ gives r² = 4r sin θ = 4y. Since r² = x² + y², x² + y² = 4y, so x² + (y − 2)² = 4. This is the circle centred at (0, 2) with radius 2.
(e) (i) Differentiate x² + (y − 2)² = 4 implicitly: 2x + 2(y − 2) dy/dx = 0. Therefore dy/dx = −x/(y − 2).
(ii) The gradient is undefined when y − 2 = 0, so y = 2. Substitution into x² + (y − 2)² = 4 gives x² = 4, hence x = ±2.
(f) The locus r = 4 sin θ is the circle x² + (y − 2)² = 4, centred at (0, 2) with radius 2. Its real-axis intercept is (0, 0); its imaginary-axis intercepts are (0, 0) and (0, 4). Sketch this circle on the Argand diagram.
(g) For r = 4 + 4 sin θ, x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ. Since dr/dθ = 4 cos θ, dx/dθ = (dr/dθ)cos θ − r sin θ = 4(1 − sin θ − 2 sin²θ), while dy/dθ = (dr/dθ)sin θ + r cos θ = 4 cos θ(1 + 2 sin θ). Therefore, wherever dx/dθ ≠ 0, dy/dx = (dy/dθ)/(dx/dθ) = cos θ(1 + 2 sin θ)/(1 − sin θ − 2 sin²θ).
(h) At A the tangent is horizontal, so dy/dx = 0. From the expression in (g), cos θ(1 + 2 sin θ) = 0. Point A is in the third quadrant and is not the top point, so cos θ ≠ 0 and 1 + 2 sin θ = 0. Thus sin θ = −1/2; in the third quadrant, θ = 7π/6.

5. [Maximum mark: 5]

The derivative of f is f′(x)=2e^(−3x). The graph passes through (1/3,5). Find f(x).
records.independentSolutionText: f(x)=−(2/3)e^(−3x)+C. Using f(1/3)=5 gives C=5+2/(3e), so f(x)=−(2/3)e^(−3x)+5+2/(3e). This agrees with the official markscheme.
